below.faq1Q: My desktop PC has no camera or microphone — how do I join a Zoom or Google Meet call?
below.faq1A: Open PhoneWebcam on your PC to generate a QR code and 4-character pairing code, scan it with your smartphone, and tap Start Camera & Mic. Your phone immediately streams crisp video and microphone audio over Wi-Fi straight to your browser. From there, share the live tab or download the 1-click OBS Studio JSON file to use your phone as a native virtual camera in Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, or Discord.
below.faq2Q: How can I use my phone's microphone on my PC for Zoom calls?
below.faq2A: PhoneWebcam automatically captures your phone microphone alongside the video stream with echo cancellation and noise suppression enabled. Local PC playback is muted by default so you don't hear room echo, while the live audio meter shows your voice level. To route your phone mic directly into Zoom or Meet, import the 1-click OBS JSON setup (which enables Control Audio via OBS) and send that audio track through a free virtual audio cable like VB-Cable.
below.faq3Q: Can I use my iPhone as a webcam on a Windows PC for free without installing an app?
below.faq3A: Yes. Because PhoneWebcam runs 100% inside your mobile and desktop web browsers, you can connect an iPhone to a Windows PC (or Mac) completely free without downloading anything from the App Store or installing PC drivers. Just open the pairing link in Safari on your iPhone and grant camera and microphone access.

below.faq4Q: Does this work with Android phones without a USB cable?
below.faq4A: Yes—Android devices connect completely wirelessly in Chrome over your local Wi-Fi network without USB cables, ADB debugging, or companion APKs. You can switch between front and rear lenses, choose 720p or 1080p, toggle the rear flashlight on supported devices, and keep your screen awake during long meetings.
below.faq5Q: How low is the latency when using a phone as a webcam over Wi-Fi?
below.faq5A: Because media streams directly peer-to-peer over your local Wi-Fi router using WebRTC instead of detouring through cloud servers, latency on a 5 GHz Wi-Fi network is typically only a few milliseconds. You can monitor the live round-trip latency and stream resolution right inside the preview toolbar.
below.faq6Q: Can I repurpose an old spare phone as a dedicated desk webcam?
below.faq6A: Absolutely. Even an older iPhone or Android smartphone usually has a far sharper camera sensor and cleaner microphone than built-in laptop webcams. Mount your old phone on a small tripod, plug it into a charger, enable Keep Screen Awake, and bookmark the Clean OBS View URL for a dedicated wireless studio camera.
below.faq7Q: Is my camera feed private? Does PhoneWebcam send video or audio to a server?
below.faq7A: Your video and microphone streams never touch a video server and are never recorded or stored. A brief signaling handshake (~2 seconds) introduces your phone and PC, after which 100% of the encrypted WebRTC video and audio travels directly between your two devices over local Wi-Fi.
